result:
The turnipfork lane is finished. No test showed a gain that only our own driver could deliver, so I built no prototype, registered no prediction and requested no driver runs. The brief's exit clause covers this outcome.

**Why the previous session stopped:** it was waiting correctly. The control test needed a driver swap that no lane can do. Meanwhile PR #318 (the Gate 0 report and the build) was merged, and the host then ran the control after that session had ended. I've written this in `docs/lanes/turnipfork/NOTES.md`. Because #318 is merged, this session's work is in a new PR, #353.

**Results:**
- **Control:** passed. Our unmodified build renders the 12 texture suites identically to T30 on all 220 captures (the host's run).
- **(g) texture-coordinate rounding** (Nova, T30, 220 captures):
  - Switching the whole device from truncation to round-to-nearest-even is worse: 21 rows better, 127 worse, and differing pixels rise from 1,408,643 to 1,426,637. Every one of the 72 cubemap rows gets worse.
  - Only 3D textures benefit. Applying it to 3D textures alone would remove at most 8,140 differing pixels (0.58%) and make two rows exact.
  - The setting is written once for the whole device (`tu6_init_static_regs`, `tu_cmd_buffer.cc:2166,2290`). A 3D-only version would need a patched driver shipped in the app, plus a fallback for non-Adreno phones. That isn't worth it for 0.58%.
  - A cheaper route may exist in our own shader, without any driver change. It is untested; I've noted it for whichever lane owns pgraph.
- **(f) tile-memory (GMEM) policy** (Crimson Skies, 240 s, two runs per setting): the default, forced system memory and forced GMEM all give a median of 29 fps with a 33.3 ms guest frame. The game runs at its 30 fps cap, so this shows no setting costs anything. It cannot show a gain.

**Where things stand:**
- The feasibility report has a new "Gate 1 results" section in `docs/investigations/adreno-driver-feasibility.md`, and NOTES record what not to repeat and what would reopen this.
- The reproducible build (`tools/turnip/build.sh`) and the host's driver-swap script stay available as tools. They're worth using again only if a profile shows GPU or driver time slowing frames in a game that isn't frame-capped.
- The summary is posted on #68 (comment 5843158832).
- `preflight.sh` passes. PR #353 is marked ready, and its `Files:` line matches the diff.
